name: Isolated DC-to-DC converter
summary: A DC/DC converter with an internal high-frequency transformer that separates input and output galvanically.
description: An isolated DC/DC converter uses a high-frequency transformer between its input and output stages, so the two DC systems have no conductive connection. Isolation lets the output be earthed differently from the input, for example a floating battery bus supplying an earthed control system, or keeps a fault on one side from reaching the other.
Drawings show the DC/DC box with a transformer mark or a pair of coupled coils inside, or a vertical double line across the box. The isolation voltage is a key rating and should be written beside it.

The symbol alone does not state the test voltage or whether the isolation is functional or reinforced for safety. Those properties decide whether the output can be treated as a separated circuit, so they must be read from the product data.
readingNotes: A transformer mark inside the box shows isolation.
Read the isolation rating rather than assuming safety separation.
drawingChecklist: State input and output voltages and isolation voltage.
distinction: An isolated converter separates input and output; a non-isolated buck or boost converter shares a common conductor.
